messages:
Marta: Heads-up — new hire ran into onboarding pain: sampleapp kept failing auth with our example env vars. Anyone else seeing REDWOOD_API_KEY vs REDWOOD_KEY ambiguity? I thought we standardized on REDWOOD_API_KEY.
Alex: Saw this yesterday. The CLI currently prefers REDWOOD_KEY if present (legacy alias). Not documented clearly in sampleapp README.
Sam: Wow — the sampleapp also sets REDWOOD_ORG in docker-compose which triggers implicit org-binding. So keys from personal workspace break.
Marta: repro steps:

```
export REDWOOD_KEY=pk_personal_abcdef
# or set REDWOOD_API_KEY=pk_personal_abcdef -> different behavior
./scripts/run-local.sh
```

Result: 403 with "key not valid for org".
Alex: Reproducer makes sense. CLI attaches org header when REDWOOD_ORG present. If key is org-scoped, personal key => mismatch.
keybot: Note: key naming alias will be deprecated on 2026-06-01 per announcements. See https://redwood.example/keys/deprecations (automated).
Sam: Short-term options:
- Update sampleapp to use REDWOOD_API_KEY only
- Add a startup check that flags when env vars mismatch (quickcheck)
- Update README with clear note about org-scoped keys
Marta: +1 for startup check. Could we add a non-fatal warning printed to console: "Detected REDWOOD_ORG + key mismatch; try using org-scoped key or unset REDWOOD_ORG"?
Alex: I can PR the startup check and README change. Will also add a small unit test for env precedence.
Sam: Can someone file a docs ticket so support doesn't get the repeated tickets? I'll create one and tag #support.
Marta: Thanks. Alex — ping me when PR is up and I'll review. Sam — thanks for the ticket.
keybot: Created ticket #INFR-894: "sampleapp: clarify key env vars and detect org/key mismatch" at 3287654388.
Alex: PR opened: https://git.example/redwood/sampleapp/pull/612, includes console warning + README tweak.
Marta: LGTM after tweak to wording. Thx.
